claim: Toska settles in the Stavanger region from summer 2003; rents a townhouse at Skjeneholen 61, Sandnes, in Nov 2003, living there with his partner and newborn son.

The tip came via criminal contacts with informants among security guards in Stavanger. A 26-year-old G4S guard met Toska several times, described the courtyard and 'the glass into the basement', drew the interior and offered to copy alarm keys; later sentenced to 3 years (2008).
conflict_or_note: The guard claims he thought it was a burglary, not a robbery.

claim: NOKAS was about to move to a new, much more secure building in spring 2004, so the gang felt they had to strike soon.

From a small atrium in the courtyard you could see straight into the counting room. Schumann: 'You see the vaults being opened at eight. You see pallets of money and know there are hundreds of millions there.'
First attempt. Toska lay in the courtyard, freezing. The operation was called off.
conflict_or_note: REASON CONFLICTS: R03 says he saw staff moving money out of the basement; R07 (Dødsranet) says Schumann's radio equipment failed and the robbers were 'deaf'. Present both, or the book's version after checking it.

claim: Toska's best friend and co-planner William Ellingsen (29) was killed by a stray bullet fired through a door after a party in Oslo. He was not the target.
Toska gave the eulogy at Ellingsen's funeral. Afterwards he decided the robbery must be 'spectacular and massive', with many more participants, to honour William.
conflict_or_note: One participant: 'the shock over William's death led to irrational thinking and planning.'

claim: Second attempt aborted: Schumann suspected police were watching his stolen semi-trailer and drove it back to Oslo; the others, dressed for the robbery in a disused slaughterhouse, spotted a red alarm light and a guard, and called it off.
conflict_or_note: Confirm in Dødsranet.

claim: Escape route from the city centre rehearsed, partly on footpaths and unfinished cycle paths; where it ran through underpasses they walked it to avoid attention.

Police received warnings from other units around end Feb/early March; a working group of fewer than 10 was set up. A 13-page intelligence document named three possible cities. On Fri 2 April police leadership put revolvers in three patrol cars instead of two.
SEFO (police complaints authority) concluded there was a 'system failure': important information was not passed to the operational officers who would face the risk.
At the morning briefing it was Arne Sigve Klungland, as field commander, who passed the intelligence on to the patrols. Officer Erik Håland: 'then I understood this was serious'.
It was Easter week; many officers were off; traffic was light because many had already left for the holidays.

7–8 robbers collected from the townhouse at Skjeneholen and driven to an assembly point in woods near Tennisland; the van returned for the rest plus mattresses, bedding and towels to be soaked in fuel and burned in the truck.
The robbers taped white armbands on their overalls: mourning bands in honour of William Ellingsen.
No battle cry, total silence as they left the assembly point; 'like a football dressing room before a decisive match'.
CCTV on Lagårdsveien records the stolen truck (07:00) and getaway cars; at 07:40 all eleven robbers are gathered, dressed and armed.
Johnny Thendrup drives a white Volvo truck with covered flatbed into the police-station driveway on Lagårdsveien and sets it alight; throws tear-gas canisters at the main entrance.
conflict_or_note: R12 gives 08:02 for the blocking.

claim: Robbers enter the courtyard via the main entrance of Handelens Hus. Sledgehammer and battering ram; the special glass does not give.

Erling Havnå, former European kickboxing champion, swings the sledgehammer, then charges with the 70 kg battering ram. Toska had insisted the pane was 'kjeks' (like a cracker) and budgeted 10–15 seconds for it.
Robbery alarm registered by Stavanger police.
conflict_or_note: R01 places the alarm after Toska's first shots, 08:03.

claim: Toska fires at the glass himself first, then fetches Schumann, who empties several AG3 magazines. Schumann: 'at least 100 shots along the edge of the window'. Then the rhythmic blows of the others, and the pane falls in, 'pulverised'.
Number of shots at the window: 113.
conflict_or_note: R01 says 'about 120'; Schumann says 'at least 100'. Use 'over a hundred' or '113' citing police count.

claim: While the robbers were stuck on the glass, three female employees in the basement moved two trolleys holding 60 million kroner into the lift. They heard Schumann's gunfire as the lift doors closed.
conflict_or_note: Strong human detail; treat with dignity, no names.

claim: First police car (officers Erik Håland and Steffen Thesen, 'Charlie 3-0', revolvers with 12 rounds each) arrives at Domkirkeplassen.
CCTV shows the first robbers inside the NOKAS premises. Klikk gives 08:09: six minutes after the first hammer blow.
The robbers had expected 300–400 million kroner and brought 15 large bags; they got mostly blue 200-kroner notes instead of 1,000s.
conflict_or_note: R07: Toska hoped for 'well over 100 million, maybe half a billion'.

claim: They tried to batter the barred gate of the main vault with the ram and failed. It later turned out the door was not locked: they could have reached in and lifted a handle from the inside.
conflict_or_note: Central irony; verify against the judgment if possible.

claim: Toska ran around inside with a watch in his hand, knowing they were far behind schedule. The plan was 7–8 minutes; it took nearly 20.
Schumann takes position at Kongsgata/Klubbgata, puts plain-clothes officer Fred Sherling on the ground: 'Who are you?'

Shoot-out across Domkirkeplassen; Håland fires 17 shots, Thesen 3; Johnny Thendrup is hit in the thigh. A passing cyclist, Olav Arnt Hopsdal, is put on the ground by a robber and believes the whole time it is the police.
Commuters, a bus, and women with prams pass by on the square as if nothing were happening; some thought it was an exercise.
Schumann fires his AG3 at the police command vehicle on Kongsgata outside the Maritim hotel. Klungland reverses, is blocked by a bus, and is hit.
conflict_or_note: LOCATION CONFLICT: R04 says he died 'in Klubbgata'. WOUND CONFLICT: head (R01, R04, R10) vs throat (R07). Script avoids wound detail anyway.

claim: Schumann says he fired low at the headlight to scare, then tried to shoot the blue light without adjusting his sight: 'the fatal mistake'. Stavanger tingrett found it was an aimed shot to stop the driver.
conflict_or_note: Present the court's finding as the fact and Schumann's claim as his claim.

claim: Klungland, 53, born 1950 in Flekkefjord; politiførstebetjent and field commander (operativ uteleder); 30 years' service: dog handler, rescue leader, trainer of police students; also drove a bus for church trips for pensioners; active in Riska; married 1977, two children.
The last of the three robbery cars leaves the square; shots are fired from all three. The Range Rover hits the Saab on the way out.
Cars set on fire at Lyse's transformer station; the first report of burning cars comes at 08:35:57. The robbers continue in two waiting cars.
conflict_or_note: PLACE: 'Sørmarka' (R08, R12) vs 'Ullandhaug' (R04) vs 'Smedheia' (R07); all are adjacent. Use 'the woods at Sørmarka'.

claim: Six robbers and all 57.4 million go to a safe-house flat in Nedre Dalgate, a few hundred metres from the square; the rest go to Toska's townhouse in Sandnes. On TV they learn a police officer has died.

DNA evidence: the truck did not burn properly (Thendrup forgot to let air into the cab, and the fire brigade next door arrived fast); the Range Rover fire was put out quickly; Toska lost an earplug with his DNA inside the counting room.
conflict_or_note: CORRECTION to our script: the 'mattresses delivered the DNA' line is supported by R02 but is only part of the story. The earplug is the stronger, more personal detail.

claim: The only photograph taken during the robbery was shot by a tourist from a hotel.
Klungland's son Kjetil, an ambulance driver, saw black smoke over Ullandhaug and thought it was a house fire; he learned at the hospital that his father had been killed.
conflict_or_note: Very sensitive. Use only with care, ideally after contacting the family.

claim: The Klungland family chose to forgive the robbers, grounded in their Christian faith; Kjetil has given talks nationwide and has had private conversations with Schumann.
conflict_or_note: Possible ending; family consent strongly advised.

claim: Toska hid in Sandnes, then Oslo; a photo of him washing the decking spread in the media; driven ~3,500 km to Huétor Santillán (Granada). His partner and baby followed until late July.
conflict_or_note: R07: partner stayed nine weeks.

claim: Several million of the loot were invested in hashish ('Operation Wonderboy'); lost when police seized over 700 kg in Asker on 29–30 Nov 2004.
conflict_or_note: R08: at least 4.3 million.

claim: Police data specialist nicknamed 'Den skarpe kniven' (the sharp knife) had 40 seconds at Oslo internet cafés to reroute traffic; a secret court order (Oct 2004) allowed monitoring of two cafés on Grünerløkka.
Toska created three addresses at postmaster.co.uk; his own was omahabeach@postmaster.co.uk.
Spanish police reach a Madrid café five minutes too late, but get a CCTV image of Toska leaving.

At Norwegian police request, Postmaster slowed login speed for all customers across Europe; Toska stayed online longer than usual, reading Norwegian news, including about the anniversary memorial for Klungland and Halimi's arrest in Kosovo.
conflict_or_note: Core dramatic irony.

claim: Toska is arrested at the Chicoti Mini Market internet café in Málaga with Danny Bungard, while the memorial for Klungland is taking place at Stavanger police station; the news spread as a murmur through the gathering.
conflict_or_note: Date settled by multiple sources: 5 April.

claim: Toska admits taking part in the robbery in Stavanger tingrett (the trial started 19 Sep 2005, held in a church congregation's hall at Forus; 232 witnesses).
conflict_or_note: Our script said he confessed via his lawyer a week after arrest (12 April 2005). Both may be true; check.

claim: Stavanger tingrett convicts all 13; Toska 19 years.
Schumann admits in Gulating lagmannsrett that he fired the shots that killed Klungland.
Gulating lagmannsrett: Toska 15 years, Schumann 13 years.
Supreme Court (HR-2007-1184-A, Rt-2007-1056): Toska 18 years; Schumann 16 years' preventive detention (forvaring), minimum 10.
conflict_or_note: R01's own text lists Toska as '19' in one place and '18' in the table; news (BT '18 års fengsel for Toska') confirms 18. CORRECTION to our script (which says 19).

claim: A NOKAS guard was sentenced to 3 years (2008). Jusuf Hani, the last robber, turned himself in in 2009; 6.5 years in 2011.

57.4 million stolen; about 5.7 million recovered from Betew's friends (the largest seizure); about 51 million still missing as of 2008–2019. The convicted are jointly liable to the insurer for 51 million.
conflict_or_note: Time-sensitive: 'still missing' as of the latest source (2019/2024).

claim: Ten years on, 32 NOKAS employees had symptoms of psychological late effects (Finansforbundet study).
Investigation and trials cost the state over 200 million kroner (some sources: over 300 million).
conflict_or_note: Conflict 200 vs 300 million.

claim: Klungland was posthumously awarded the Politiets hederskors (2005); a bronze plaque in his memory was unveiled in Stavanger in 2006. Funeral in Stavanger Cathedral on 14 April 2004, attended by about 600 police officers, with a helicopter flying low over the city.
Toska was a relatively talented chess player as a teenager; in 2022 TV 2 used him as a guest in its chess studio.
conflict_or_note: Supports the chess motif as fact rather than pure metaphor.

claim: NRK calls the final phase of the hunt 'a chess game between the Sharp Knife and the so-called Mastermind', a nickname the media gave Toska after the robbery.
conflict_or_note: Gives the chess motif its payoff: the police out-play the chess player.

claim: The 13 defendants were sentenced to a combined 181 years of prison or preventive detention in Stavanger tingrett.
conflict_or_note: CONFLICT: R02 (en.wiki) gives Toska 21 years in the district court; R01, R17 give 19 (possibly 21 includes other cases). Script uses only the final 18 (F54).

claim: Toska released on parole after serving 13 years.
conflict_or_note: MONTH CONFLICT: May 2018 (R13) vs July 2018 (R15, citing VG 13 Jul 2018). Say '2018' only.

claim: Schumann released on parole in 2014, finally released September 2019.
conflict_or_note: Not needed in the script unless the ending widens.

claim: Toska was arrested on the anniversary, 'one year and seven hours' after the robbery.
conflict_or_note: Strong line if confirmed; R17 confirms 'the day one year after the robbery'.
